title: SDK kitchen-scripts: curated examples for Next.js, FastAPI, Go HTTP server and CLI
creator: Marco Liu
description: Create a small set of opinionated, well-documented example apps (Next.js SSR streaming, FastAPI async server, Go HTTP server with context cancellation, and a CLI that surfaces streaming + retry ergonomics). The goal is to provide copy-paste ready patterns for customers and internal teams showing best-practices for: streaming handling, retry/backoff policies, idempotency, token-level cost instrumentation, graceful downgrade strategies, and resume/cancellation flows.
acceptance_criteria: Four runnable example repos/workspaces (nextjs, fastapi, go-http, cli) with README and quickstart
Each example demonstrates the SDK's recommended streaming helper API and retry guidance
Automated tests (smoke) that exercise streaming + cancellation and non-streaming retries
Docs/Confluence page summarizing trade-offs and recommended defaults
Design review sign-off from DX and Runtime teams
implementation_notes: Main design: provide a thin adapter layer per language that exports two primitives: `stream` (pushes chunks to a callback/AsyncIterator) and `generate` (returns a single result with deterministic retry semantics). Default retry policy: idempotent GET-like reads should use exponential backoff with jitter; non-idempotent streaming responses will not be auto-retried — instead we provide a `checkpoint` helper to emit partial results and an option to `resume` using a deterministic prefix key. Telemetry: emit token_count, latency_ms, model_variant, and cost_estimate tags to the Console. For Next.js example prefer streaming SSR via server components / edge where available. FastAPI example will use asyncio background tasks for long polls and a WebSocket example for real-time. Go example must demonstrate context cancellation and minimal memory KV cache wiring. CLI shows both blocking and streaming modes with a `--resume` flag and clear UX for retries.
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Opted to NOT implement automatic retries for mid-stream failures because it hides partial state from callers and breaks streaming-first UX
Expose `retryable` wrapper for idempotent operations where SDK can safely retry under the hood
Provide recommended batch sizes per language but leave them configurable; users with strict latency SLOs can reduce batch window
Decided to use a single helper naming convention across SDKs: `stream_*` for streaming helpers and `call_*` for request/response helpers to aid discoverability
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: customers copy examples verbatim and hit scaling/cost issues. Mitigation: include cost-estimate guidance in each README and instrument the examples to show token/cost counters
Risk: language parity drift across SDKs. Mitigation: include cross-language Lint in CI and a weekly parity smoke job
Risk: resumed streams can cause duplicate tokens. Mitigation: implement idempotency prefix and guidance to dedupe on application side
